summary: @servicetitan/startup-mfe-compat preinstall downloads Bun runtime to execute bundled obfuscated payload
details: The package's declared preinstall script (`node setup.mjs`) probes for a local `bun` binary and, if absent, downloads the Bun runtime from a GitHub release, extracts it to a temp directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it against a bundled 727KB obfuscated file `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a single-line obfuscator.io-style bundle (large numeric/string constant array, string-array rotation shuffler, hex-named identifiers) whose contents cannot be inspected without execution. Fetching an alternate JavaScript runtime at install time solely to execute a sibling obfuscated script is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern: arbitrary code runs on any host that runs `npm install`, and it runs under a non-Node runtime that bypasses Node-based registry scanners. The package presents itself under the `@servicetitan/*` scope with a homepage at `docs.st.dev` while shipping this dropper, which is inconsistent with a legitimate frontend micro-frontend compatibility library.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
